description: Held-out questions over the same 26 synthetic resumes as the retrieval benchmark. Used only to recalibrate the 'not found' similarity cutoff (ask.NOT_FOUND_THRESHOLD) and to check the LLM judge (eval/answer_eval_protocol.md). No question repeats or paraphrases a benchmark question; `python -m eval.golden validate` checks for obvious overlap. Answerable questions are labelled with the benchmark's labelling_rules; each unanswerable question says why no resume answers it.
labelling_rules: The labelling_rules of eval/retrieval_benchmark.json apply unchanged.
judge_check_rules: Each answerable question has one good and one flawed answer, written from its labelled chunks. Citation numbers [n] refer to the question's labels in order: [1] is the first label.
A good answer states every label's fact and cites the label that supports each claim.

A flawed answer has exactly one kind of flaw: omission (a labelled candidate is left out), invented_claim (a claim no excerpt supports) or wrong_citation (a true claim cites an excerpt that does not support it).

judge_check.flawed_answer: Michael Chen [1], Priya Nair [2] and Emma Thompson [3] each hold a Master's in Data Science.
judge_check.flaw_note: Sara Okafor (MSc Data Science) is left out.
